hints: Use the horizontal motion to find the speed $v$ at the bottom of the slope: the kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ equals the work done against resistance $250 \times 1.05\text{ J}$.
Calculate the normal contact force on the slope: $R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 35(10)\cos 30^\circ$.
Write the work-energy balance for the sloping section: potential energy lost ($mgh$) equals kinetic energy gained ($\frac{1}{2}mv^2$) plus work done against friction ($F \times 2.5$).
Substitute $F = \mu R$ into the equation and solve for $\mu$.
walkthrough:
Use the work-energy relation on the horizontal section to find the speed $v$ at the bottom of the incline:
$$\frac{1}{2}(35)v^2 = 250(1.05) = 262.5\text{ J}$$
$$v^2 = \frac{2 \times 262.5}{35} = \frac{525}{35} = 15$$

Calculate the normal contact force on the $30^\circ$ slope:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 35(10)\cos 30^\circ = 350\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 175\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 303.11\text{ N}$$

Apply the work-energy principle for motion down the $2.5\text{ m}$ sloping section:
$$\text{PE loss} = \text{KE gain} + \text{Work against friction}$$
$$mg(2.5\sin 30^\circ) = \frac{1}{2}(35)v^2 + F(2.5)$$
$$35(10)(1.25) = 262.5 + 2.5F$$
$$437.5 = 262.5 + 2.5F$$

Solve for the friction force $F$ and coefficient of friction $\mu$:
$$2.5F = 437.5 - 262.5 = 175 \implies F = \frac{175}{2.5} = 70\text{ N}$$
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{70}{175\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2}{5\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{15} \approx 0.231$$

teacher_walkthrough:
First, determine the kinetic energy and speed squared of the child at the transition from the sloping section to the horizontal section. The child travels $1.05\text{ m}$ on the horizontal surface against resistance of $250\text{ N}$ before coming to rest:
$$W_{\text{res, horizontal}} = 250 \times 1.05 = 262.5\text{ J}$$
By the work-energy principle on the flat section, the kinetic energy at the bottom must equal this work:
$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 262.5\text{ J}$$
Substitute $m = 35\text{ kg}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(35)v^2 = 262.5$$
$$17.5 v^2 = 262.5$$
$$v^2 = \frac{262.5}{17.5} = 15$$

Calculate the normal contact force $R$ perpendicular to the $30^\circ$ slope:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = (35)(10)\cos 30^\circ = 350\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 175\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 303.109\text{ N}$$

State the limiting friction force on the slope in terms of the unknown coefficient of friction $\mu$:
$$F = \mu R = 175\sqrt{3}\mu$$

Apply the work-energy principle for the motion of the child descending the $2.5\text{ m}$ rough slope from rest:
$$\text{PE loss} = \text{KE gain} + W_{\text{friction}}$$
Compute the potential energy loss over vertical descent $h = 2.5\sin 30^\circ = 1.25\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = (35)(10)(1.25) = 437.5\text{ J}$$
Substitute the known quantities:
$$437.5 = 262.5 + F(2.5)$$
Subtract $262.5$ from both sides:
$$2.5 F = 437.5 - 262.5$$
$$2.5 F = 175$$
Divide by $2.5$:
$$F = \frac{175}{2.5} = 70\text{ N}$$

Use the friction relationship $F = \mu R$ to solve for $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{70}{175\sqrt{3}}$$
Divide numerator and denominator by $35$:
$$\mu = \frac{2}{5\sqrt{3}}$$
Rationalise the denominator by multiplying top and bottom by $\sqrt{3}$:
$$\mu = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5 \times 3} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{15}$$
Evaluate as a decimal:
$$\mu \approx \frac{2(1.73205)}{15} = \frac{3.4641}{15} \approx 0.23094$$
Rounding to three significant figures:
$$\mu = 0.231$$
Thus the coefficient of friction is $0.231$ (or $\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{15}$).
